RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-40E31914E1-52376
Member: Sawyer Iverson (ID W821798872)
Requested Service: Knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy, CPT 29881
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-02
Appeal Deadline: 2027-01-29

To the Grievance and Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29881 (arthroscopy, knee, surgical, with meniscectomy). The denial notice states the reason for the determination as: "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am submitting this letter, together with my complete clinical records, to address that stated basis for denial directly.

I understand that MHS/Ambetter delegates review of knee and other musculoskeletal surgical requests to Evolent, and that Evolent's Clinical Guideline for Knee Arthroscopy (Guideline Number Evolent_CG_1764) sets out the "General Requirements" that apply to elective knee arthroscopic surgery. Below I address each General Requirement element I was able to identify in that guideline and show where the record documents it. I have not been able to obtain the guideline's specific "Meniscectomy/Meniscal Repair" indications subsection, and I am not quoting or attributing any language to the plan for that subsection; I address that portion of my case in my own words below and specifically request that the plan provide me the full text of that subsection.

1. Clinical correlation of subjective complaints with objective findings and imaging
The guideline requires: "There is clinical correlation of the individual's subjective complaints with objective exam findings and/or imaging (when applicable)."
My record satisfies this directly: physical examination on file documents positive provocative testing on the affected knee and range of motion limited by pain, and MRI performed 2026-05-30 confirms a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking, with preserved articular cartilage (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1). My reported symptoms of locking and giving way are directly corroborated by this imaging finding and exam.

2. Documented loss of function
The guideline requires: "Knee pain with documented loss of function: Deviation from normal knee function which may include painful weight bearing and/or inadequate range of motion (> 10 degrees flexion contracture or < 110 degrees flexion or both) to accomplish age-appropriate activities of daily living (ADLs), occupational or athletic requirements)."
My record documents 14 months of progressive knee pain unrelieved by rest, with mechanical locking and giving way, inability to squat or kneel, and function limited to level walking only. This represents a clear deviation from normal knee function affecting activities of daily living.

3. Medical stability/optimization for surgery
The guideline requires: "Individual is medically stable and optimized for surgery, and any treatable comorbidities are adequately medically managed such as diabetes, nicotine addiction, or an excessively high BMI."
I am a non-smoker with a BMI of 29, which is not an excessively high BMI, and I have no other documented comorbidity requiring further optimization.

4. No active infection
The guideline requires: "Individual does not have an active local or systemic infection." My record confirms no active infection.

5. No untreated drug dependency
The guideline requires: "Individual does not have active, untreated drug dependency (including but not limited to narcotics, opioids, or muscle relaxants) unless engaged in a treatment program." My record confirms no untreated substance use.

6. Timing of intra-articular injection
The guideline requires: "No intra-articular cortisone injections within 4 weeks of surgery." My corticosteroid injection was administered on 2026-04-19. More than four weeks have elapsed since that injection as of the date of this appeal and as of the original prior-authorization request, so this requirement is met.

7. Required content of clinical notes
The guideline states: "Clinical notes should address: Symptom onset, duration, and severity; Loss of function and/or limitations; Type and duration of non-operative management modalities (where applicable)." All three elements are documented in the enclosed records: 14 months of progressive, unrelieved pain (onset/duration/severity); locking, giving way, inability to squat or kneel, and restriction to level walking (loss of function); and 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy (18 visits, 2026-02-25 through 2026-06-17), 4 months of NSAID therapy, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-19 (type and duration of non-operative management).

8. Non-operative management requirement
The guideline states: "Unless otherwise stated in the subsections below, non-operative management must include at least TWO or more of the following, unless otherwise specified: Rest or activity modifications/limitations; Ice/heat; Protected weight bearing; Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics, tramadol; Brace/orthosis; Physical therapy modalities; Supervised home exercise; Weight optimization; Injections: corticosteroid, NSAID, viscosupplementation."
My record documents at least three distinct modalities: (a) supervised physical therapy/home exercise (16 weeks, 18 visits, focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion), (b) pharmacologic treatment (NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief), and (c) injection therapy (corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-19, yielding only 3 weeks of partial relief). This exceeds the "at least TWO" requirement.

Meniscectomy-specific indications
I was not able to obtain the text of the guideline's specific "Meniscectomy/Meniscal Repair" indications subsection, and I am not attributing any language to the plan for that portion of the criteria. In my own words: my MRI shows a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus causing mechanical locking, which is a mechanical, surgically-correctable problem that would not be expected to resolve with further conservative care, and which I understand is generally recognized in orthopedic practice as a standard indication for meniscectomy or meniscal repair, particularly where — as here — a full course of conservative treatment (physical therapy, NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injection) has already failed to relieve symptoms or the locking. I respectfully request that the plan identify, and provide me a copy of, the specific "Meniscectomy/Meniscal Repair" criteria it applied to my case so that I and my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, can confirm that every element is addressed in the enclosed records, and so that I can supplement the record if any specific element remains unaddressed.

Enclosed records
1. Physical therapy discharge summary (2026-02-25 to 2026-06-17, 18 visits)
2. Medication/treatment history documenting NSAID trial (4 months) and corticosteroid injection (2026-04-19)
3. MRI report dated 2026-05-30
4. Office examination notes documenting provocative testing and range-of-motion findings
5. Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Reyes, orthopedic surgery [to be attached]
6. [Any additional records referenced but not listed above, if applicable]

I am filing this appeal within the 180-calendar-day window stated in the denial notice (by 2027-01-29). Please confirm receipt of this appeal, and provide written notice of your determination within the timeframe required for this type of appeal. If this appeal is not resolved in my favor, I intend to pursue external review by an Independent Review Organization as permitted under my plan.

Please contact me at [phone number] or [email address] with any questions or if any additional information is needed to complete this review.

Sincerely,

Sawyer Iverson
